definition.question: What are complementarianism and egalitarianism?
definition.html:
Complementarianism is the view that men and women are equal before God as persons but given distinct roles, so that headship in marriage and "some governing and teaching roles within the church" belong to men. Its classic statement is the Danvers Statement of the Council on Biblical Manhood and Womanhood (1987 to 1988). Egalitarianism is the view that Scripture teaches "the full equality of men and women in Creation and in Redemption," opens every ministry to both, and calls husbands and wives to mutual submission, as set out in Christians for Biblical Equality's Men, Women, and Biblical Equality (1989).

In church life the question usually comes down to whether women can be pastors or elders. A third view, sometimes called soft complementarianism or the third way, reserves the pastoral office for men while opening most other teaching and leadership roles to women. See where churches stand and short answers to common questions.

faq.label: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.title: Men, Women and the Church, Briefly Answered

items.a: Complementarianism holds that men and women are "equal before God as persons and distinct in their manhood and womanhood," and that this distinction shapes their roles. In marriage it teaches the husband's "loving, humble headship"; in the church it holds that "some governing and teaching roles within the church are restricted to men," citing texts such as 1 Timothy 2:11 to 15. The words are from the Danvers Statement, drafted in December 1987 and published in final form in November 1988.

Christian egalitarianism holds that the Bible teaches "the full equality of men and women in Creation and in Redemption," that the Holy Spirit gives gifts "without preference as to gender," and that husbands and wives live in "mutual submission." It reads Galatians 3:28 as central and reads the few texts that appear to restrict women in light of "the broader teaching of Scripture and their total context." The founding statement is Christians for Biblical Equality's Men, Women, and Biblical Equality, first presented in July 1989.

items.q: What is soft complementarianism, or the third way?
items.a: It is a position between the two: the office of pastor or elder is reserved for men, but women may teach, lead and serve in most other roles. It has no founding statement of its own, but survey data show it is where many churches stand. In Lifeway Research's 2021 survey of Protestant pastors, 44% of evangelical pastors said a woman could be senior pastor at their church, while 84% said a woman could teach a coed adult Bible study. See the chart.

Among evangelical bodies, the Assemblies of God, the Church of the Nazarene, the Foursquare Church, the Evangelical Covenant Church, ECO, the Wesleyan Church and the Free Methodist Church USA ordain women as pastors. The Southern Baptist Convention, the PCA, the OPC, the Lutheran Church Missouri Synod and Acts 29 restrict the office to men. The Evangelical Free Church of America does not ordain women but leaves elders to each church; the Anglican Church in North America leaves women priests to each diocese; the Christian Reformed Church lets each congregation decide. Each is checked against its own documents in Where churches stand.

items.q: Did the Southern Baptist Convention ban women pastors?
items.a: Its confession already limits "the office of pastor/elder/overseer" to men (Baptist Faith and Message 2000, Article VI, amended in 2023). The fight since then has been over writing a ban into the SBC constitution, which takes a two-thirds vote at two consecutive annual meetings. The Law amendment got 61.45 percent on its second vote in 2024 and failed; a new amendment got 60.74% in 2025 and failed. In June 2026 the broader Truth and Unity Amendment, which also covers women preaching on Sunday mornings, passed its first vote with 74.6%. It needs a second two-thirds vote at the 2027 meeting. See the vote chart.

It depends on the church. The PCA and the OPC restrict deacons, like elders, to men. The Southern Baptist confession lists pastor and deacon as the two offices but limits only the pastoral office to men. In Lifeway Research's 2021 survey, 56% of evangelical pastors and 79% of mainline pastors said a woman could be a deacon at their church; among Baptist pastors it was 29%.

items.q: Which Bible passages are at the center of the debate?
items.a: Complementarians lean on Genesis 2, 1 Corinthians 11:2 to 16, Ephesians 5:21 to 33 and especially 1 Timothy 2:11 to 15 with the elder qualifications of 1 Timothy 3 and Titus 1. Egalitarians lean on Genesis 1:26 to 28, Galatians 3:28, Pentecost in Acts 2, and the women Paul names as coworkers, such as Phoebe and Junia in Romans 16; they read 1 Corinthians 14:34 to 35 and 1 Timothy 2 as dealing with "specific, local problems," in the words of the Assemblies of God's 2010 position paper. The 1 Timothy 2 reading in our curated list shows how much rests on a single passage.
